thread:
jamie: seeing a surge of 502s and pod restarts in eu-west4 gpupool since 09:10 UTC. kernel logs show conntrack evictions on several nodes. pods losing connections mid-request. anyone oncall with bandwidth?
infra-bot: ALERT: conntrack pressure high on nodes [ip-10-3-45-12, ip-10-3-45-13, ip-10-3-46-07] nf_conntrack_count=565432 nf_conntrack_max=600000 -> eviction events detected
alex: which pods are failing? are these inference workers or prefetchers? any IPs or patterns from tcpdump?
jamie: mostly inference-worker-* and a few tensorflow-prefetcher pods. attaching short log snippet:```kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet (evicted)
Sep 14 09:12:03 ip-10-3-45-12 kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet```
jamie: conntrack dump stats from node ip-10-3-45-12: `conntrack -L | wc -l` -> 567003; `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max` -> 600000
rita: ugh. likely prefetchers opened lots of short lived outbound connections to cache/model store and exhausted ephemeral+conntrack. short-term: bump nf_conntrack_max and scale down prefetchers. medium-term: reduce SNAT churn or move prefetchers to a no-snat subnet.
sophia: also check tcp_tw_reuse/recycle and reduce TIME_WAIT if safe for our stack. RDMA/RoCE not involved here (this pool is non-roce).
alex: can we do quick mitigations? increase nf_conntrack_max to 1M on affected nodes, and scale prefetchers to 0 for 10m to let table drain?
jamie: applying sysctl to the three worst nodes now: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=1000000` and kube-proxy restart targeted to those nodes. scaling prefetcher deployment (eu-west4) replicas 12 -> 2 now.
infra-bot: EVENT: manual sysctl applied on [ip-10-3-45-12, ip-10-3-45-13, ip-10-3-46-07] by jamie. kube-proxy restart jobs queued.
jamie: early signal: conntrack count dropped to ~420k across cluster, 502s reduced from ~200/min to ~15/min. one node (ip-10-3-45-12) still showing high evictions, investigating further.
alex: good improvement. can we cordon that node and drain to inspect without causing more impact?
jamie: planning to cordon ip-10-3-45-12 in 5m, will tcpdump for SYN flood pattern before draining: `tcpdump -i eth0 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn) != 0' -w /tmp/syn-spike.pcap`
rita: taking ownership of capturing conntrack state dump as well: `conntrack -L > /tmp/conntrack-dump.txt` before we flush. jamie do the tcpdump, rita will grab conntrack dump.
jamie: started capture, 60s capture saved and uploaded to s3://redwood-debug/eu-west4/syn-spike-1912345678.pcap
sophia: looked at the pcap briefly: lots of SYNs from a handful of pods (tensorflow-prefetcher-12, -15). high ephemeral port reuse latency -> many half-open sockets. not a cloud-side DDoS.
alex: action items: 1) short-term: keep nf_conntrack_max=1M and keep prefetchers scaled at 2 for 1 hour (owner: jamie). 2) medium-term: request cloud increase SNAT pool + investigate EIP-per-node or egress NAT gateway (owner: rita). 3) long-term: architectural: move prefetchers to dedicated subnet with egress that avoids SNAT (owner: platform).
jamie: cordoned and drained ip-10-3-45-12, found local prefetcher process stuck opening connections (PID 2345) — killed. collecting logs and will follow up with the model infra owners.
infra-bot: INCIDENT: downgraded to LOW impact at 09:58 UTC; monitoring continues.
jamie: current status: error rate back to baseline for most services. leaving nf_conntrack_max increased and scheduling a ticket for infra to bake permanent kernel tuning + runbook updates.
sophia: note for the runbook: include steps to identify SYN-heavy clients (`ss -s`, `conntrack -L`, tcpdump filters), and the mitigation matrix (scale down client, bump conntrack_max, cordon+drain node, flush conntrack if necessary).
alex: please add owner/ETA for cloud SNAT increase request in the ticket.
jamie: created GH issue infra/conntrack-eu-west4-2026 with details and uploads (pcap, dumps). assigning rita for cloud request, ETA 72h.
rita: acked, will open cloud support case and loop in networking.
jamie: thanks all. will keep thread updated if anything regresses. :thumbsup:
